title: Opening at the Onyx: tripling with the Roxy, and the seven-day week
summary: They doubled at the Roxy Theater and sometimes tripled with a radio show, were booked by Consolidated Radio Artists, and worked seven days a week as nobody had days off then.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And little did you know that this was going to be like a turning point in your career.
No, I thought what could it be, you know.
Yeah.

So we come down and did that. Now, while we're here, we get to go into the Roxy, we double in the Roxy Theater, and then one time we was tripling. We was playing the Roxy Theater and the Onyx and doing the Lucidin Show.
Did stuff have -- what office -- did an office have him?
That was Consolidated Radio Artists.
Oh, I don't know them.
Which was Charlie Green.
Oh.
Yeah, he used to have -- you know, Ryan. Remember Babs and her brothers?
Yes.
Well, he used to handle all of that, you know, and -- well, he was in the Brill Building at that time,
and then later on they moved into the RCA Building. It was a pretty good office. He had some pretty good things. He booked Lil, too.
Oh, did he?

Yeah, be booked Lil when I was with her. It was a pretty big office at one time. I don't know what they're doing now. I haven't heard of them lately. But we went in there, and now we're working there, and at this time you didn't get Sunday off. There was no such thing as a day off. You worked seven days.
Is that right?
Sure. Back in them days nobody got a day off.
They didn't, huh?
You worked seven days, not unless you was in maybe radio or studio musicians or something.
Is that right.
